short: A hyperbolic group that is not CAT(0)

title.title: A hyperbolic group with no geometric CAT(0) action
title.subtitle: Claim: a hyperbolic group that acts geometrically on no proper CAT(0) space, in any dimension

beats.text: Schematic: free, surface and cubulated hyperbolic groups all act on CAT(0) spaces
Gromov asked whether every hyperbolic group acts geometrically on one
The claim: one does not, and it has a finite 2-dimensional classifying space

achievement.label: Gromov's question: is every hyperbolic group CAT(0)?
statement: \exists\, G \text{ hyperbolic with no geometric CAT(0) action}
achievement.context: Before: CAT(0) known for free, surface, cubulated and low-density random groups
achievement.note: Consistent with family 252: both point to a non-cubulated world

verify.detail: Main theorem in Lean; the witness's 2-dimensionality and metric exclusion are not
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean docs and allowed axioms; we did not build it

sources.quote: There is a finite connected 2-dimensional aspherical simplicial complex K with a linear isoperimetric inequality (so pi_1 K is hyperbolic) such that pi_1 K admits no proper cocompact isometric action on any proper complete CAT(0) space, in any dimension
Gromov's question whether every hyperbolic group is CAT(0) (or CAT(-1))
Known CAT(0) for many classes (free, surface, cubulated, random groups at low density via Ollivier-Wise).
Combined with 252 (a non-residually-finite hyperbolic group) it is consistent
but the 2-dimensionality of the witness and the locally-CAT(0) metric exclusion are not included per the Lean doc.
only `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice` for every family here

plain: A group that is negatively curved from far away, yet cannot act nicely on any nonpositively curved space

steps: Suppose the group acted nicely on a CAT(0) space
Take a limiting configuration of least energy
That configuration contradicts how the complex was built

voice.text: Free, surface and cubulated groups all act on CAT zero spaces. Gromov asked about all.
Any such action would yield a limiting energy configuration, which is impossible.
Claimed: one hyperbolic group never does.
